Order here reflects DoFlow's two tracked scopes; the documented third, finer-grained JIT tier is omitted. hooks.note: kiro-cli reads hooks from an agent config's `hooks` array (agentSpawn, userPromptSubmit, preToolUse, postToolUse, stop). A preToolUse hook that exits 2 blocks the tool call; any other non-zero exit warns and allows; stop is not blockable on 2.x. DoFlow writes three preToolUse hooks (pre-implementation-gate on `write`, pre-bash-guard on `shell`, mcp-tool-guard on `*`) into every rendered agent, plus agentSpawn (session context) and stop (stop-check) on the doflow agent only. The Kiro front doors translate Kiro tool names, KIRO_SESSION_ID and assistant_response to the canonical payload before running the shared policies. `.kiro/hooks/doflow.json` (flat `{version, hooks: [...]}`, PascalCase triggers) is read by the Kiro IDE and by CLI V3 (for every agent); CLI 2.x does not read it. Kiro CLI V3 also loads standalone `.kiro/hooks/*.json` (workspace) and `~/.kiro/hooks/*.json` (global) for every agent, alongside agent-profile hooks, so doflow.json runs for all agents there, and with `--agent doflow` on V3 the preToolUse checks run twice (accepted, idempotent). V3 payloads carry `session_id`, and V3 built-in tool IDs include `read_file`, `execute_bash`, `execute_pwsh`, `fs_write`, `fs_append`, `str_replace` and `delete_file`; the front doors map the write family to Write and `execute_pwsh` to Bash, and V3 MCP IDs (`mcp_<server>_<tool>`) reach mcp-tool-guard unchanged. doflow.json scopes the MCP guard with the V3 `@mcp` selector. V3 Stop: exit 0 finishes, exit 0 with stdout JSON `{"decision":"block","reason":"..."}` starts another turn, exit 1 also starts another turn, and exit 2 does not block; the stop front door therefore turns the policy's deny into that JSON block when the payload has a session_id and keeps exit 2 with stderr for 2.x, where any non-zero exit only warns. It is not in Kiro v3's untrusted-workspace exclusion list; an untrusted workspace asks before every shell command, and whether that covers hook commands is undocumented. Observed on CLI V3 (kiro-cli 2.27.1 --v3, 2026-10-11): PreToolUse payloads carry session_id, tool_name execute_bash with tool_input.command, fs_write and str_replace with tool_input.path; the Stop payload carries only session_id, hook_event_name and cwd, with no response text or transcript path, so stop-check's unfinished-work scan has nothing to read on V3 and allows the stop.
